test_cases.name: Valid Expense Addition
test_cases.scenario: Adding an expense with a valid category and date.
test_cases.notes: The expense is added correctly when the category exists.

test_cases.name: Invalid Category Expense Addition
test_cases.scenario: Adding an expense with a non-existent category.
test_cases.expected: Error message is printed, and expense is not added.
test_cases.notes: The code prints an error but does not prevent adding the expense if the category is invalid.

test_cases.name: Empty Category Addition
test_cases.expected: Category is added as an empty string.
test_cases.notes: The code allows adding an empty string as a category.

test_cases.name: Duplicate Category Addition
test_cases.scenario: Adding a category that already exists.
test_cases.notes: The set data structure prevents duplicates, which is expected behavior.

test_cases.name: Calculate Monthly Totals with No Expenses
test_cases.scenario: Calculating totals for a month with no expenses.
test_cases.notes: The method correctly returns an empty dictionary when there are no expenses.

test_cases.name: Invalid Date Format
test_cases.scenario: Adding an expense with an invalid date format.
test_cases.expected: Error raised due to invalid date format.
test_cases.notes: The code does not handle invalid date formats and will raise a ValueError.

bugs_found: The add_expense method does not prevent adding an expense if the category is invalid.
The code does not handle invalid date formats, which can cause runtime errors.
Adding an empty string as a category is allowed, which may not be intended.
